ceiling_statement: FROZEN GUARANTEE. Maximum auditability is: every trusted output ships with a certificate binding it, via collision-resistant hash commitments, to the COMPLETE closure of its derivation (source bytes, code identity, pinned toolchain identity, configuration, ordering schedule), such that an independent third party holding only the certificate and the committed closure can, fully offline and with zero producer trust, verify that the output is the unique derivation result — by either of two EQUALLY MAXIMAL modes under the same hash-assumption family: (a) byte-identical RECOMPUTATION and comparison, or (b) checking a TRANSPARENT proof-of-recomputation (STARK-class: no trusted setup; soundness on hash-family assumptions already accepted for the commitments). Auditability terminates at the commitment boundary: nothing outside the committed closure (e.g., what the publisher's server really served at capture time) is auditable in principle — the strongest attainable is a signed/witnessed/channel-attested capture receipt committing the bytes at ingestion. COST clause (RESOURCE_BOUNDED): linear-cost recomputation is the operative verification cost only for a declared toolchain lacking an arithmetization of its pipeline; a transparent proof toolchain strictly lowers verifier cost with no assurance loss.
derivation: Verification theory admits exactly two zero-trust offline verification modes: recompute-and-compare, and proof-checking. The v1 dismissal of mode (b) is corrected on two counts: (1) it rested on a false cryptographic premise — transparent (STARK-class) proof systems have NO trusted setup; their assumptions are collision-resistant hashing, the same family the ceilings already accept for SHA-256 commitments — so mode (b) adds no new trust CATEGORY, only a proof-system soundness reduction within the same family; (2) 'arithmetizing the pipeline is infeasible' is a toolchain/cost fact, which may not appear inside an ABSOLUTE label — it is carved into the RESOURCE_BOUNDED cost clause. H8's semantic content is zero producer trust; both modes satisfy it and are equally maximal in assurance, so 'recompute-and-compare is the ceiling' is restated as 'derivability-from-committed-bytes under stated assumptions is the ceiling, attained by either mode'. The boundary claim is information-theoretic and stands: two histories producing identical committed byte-closures are indistinguishable to any auditor; past states of external sources are not replayable, hence capture receipts (signed, witnessed, or channel-attested per AX-04) are the maximum for origin bytes. Completeness of the closure is capped by what was committed — an audit is exactly as strong as the closure is total.
ceiling_kind: ABSOLUTE (assurance clause: audit knowledge bounded by the committed closure under stated hash assumptions) / RESOURCE_BOUNDED (cost clause)
lean_obligation: Theorem (verification at the ceiling): given injective-on-domain commitment H and pure derivation f, for all closures c and outputs o: Verify(cert(c,o), c) = true iff f(c) = o — stated for BOTH verifier modes, with the proof-checking mode's soundness reducing to the same collision-resistance hypothesis (mode-equivalence lemma: the two verifiers accept the same set of (c,o) pairs). Corollary (audit factorization): committedClosure(h1) = committedClosure(h2) implies auditVerdict(h1) = auditVerdict(h2) — the audit relation factors through the commitment.

attainment_witness_appendix.candidate_mechanism: Generalize the pattern the B0 witness already runs: one release-closure certificate = Merkle root (merkle-authority.lisp) over {corpus fingerprint, toolchain manifest, all committed input bytes, all output bytes, gate-plenary manifest}, hashed through hash-authority.lisp, sealed by the Ed25519 chain. Verifier: the recompute-and-compare engine (authority-evidence-replay.lisp) plus release-spine.lisp extended to recompute the WHOLE closure with per-step before/after hash-chain checks (closing the consolidation aggregate-only weakness). The transparent-proof mode is a declared-resource option: no arithmetization of the SBCL pipeline exists in the declared toolchain — recorded here as the resource fact grounding the cost clause; succinct proofs for update-validity predicates over bounded structures (proof-carrying CRDT constructions) are implemented in the literature and are admissible evidence that the cost floor is toolchain-relative.
attainment_witness_appendix.b0_gap_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: verification is spread across several seats instead of one closure certificate; some byte-identity claims are asserted in comments/tests, not recomputed; wall-clock leaks into artifacts unless frozen (couples to AX-14); consolidation replay verifies aggregates only; origin bytes enter un-attested, so the commitment boundary is weaker than the attainable capture-receipt boundary.
